text:
The meeting addressed Item 26, a report from Development Services recommending the approval of the fiscal year 2022 Action Plan and substantial amendments for the Citywide program. The item also sought authorization for the city manager to execute necessary documents with the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

Due to the late hour, the Vice Mayor requested a brief summary of the amendments rather than a full presentation. Christopher Coons explained that the report covers federal funds used for poverty alleviation and community support, representing an implementation and amendment of the five-year comprehensive plan. Patrick detailed that all ongoing programs from the current cycle would continue. However, because not all funds were spent in certain programs, the proposal reallocates approximately $1.5 million. These funds are to be set aside for the acquisition of a housing site, making them available to developers to create an affordable housing site.

No public comment was received for Item 26. Councilwoman Mongo praised the Development Services team, while Councilmember Urunga expressed anticipation for significant changes in the next five-year update. Both council members offered positive remarks to Christopher Coons and Patrick. The council then voted on the motion, which carried with eight votes in favor and zero against. Following the approval, the meeting proceeded to Item 27.
